source.title: PowerSecV: LLM-Based Secure and Low-Power Verilog Generation via Hardware-CWE Knowledge Graph and Power Evolution

review.scope: Compare RTL structure and documented assumptions with the paper's abbreviated CSR case.

notes: This replaces the former real-model counter example; its passed verification logs do not apply to these files.
The secure variant follows Figure 4(b)'s permission check and per-request auxiliary XOR register.
The low-power variant follows Figure 4(c)'s buffer and conditional array-update intent, with aligned data/address/permission metadata.
The low-power variant adds one cycle of write-commit latency and assumes accepted authorization remains valid for that transaction.
An upstream decoder must ensure consistent permissions for addresses that alias the same low-7-bit physical storage index; this is not a complete RISC-V CSR decoder.
No equality of physical waveforms, side-channel protection or power reduction has been measured or established.
